purpose: Accumulated positive AND negative knowledge about the original toolchain. Read before any compiler-sensitive reasoning. Do not retest a FALSIFIED/NON_DISCRIMINATING entry under its stated conditions unless new evidence invalidates them; cite the id instead. Routine function recovery keeps the CANONICAL profile fixed; only supervisor-launched, control-preserving experiments may challenge it.

controls.accepted_c: All src/*.c with recipes (31 functions as of 2026-09-25): is_facing_camera, rect_adjust_from_point, mat_mul_vector2, init_carstate_from_simd, rect_* family, audio*/audioresource_*, locate_*, file_combine_and_find, set_frame_callback, shape3d_init_shape, copy_string, toupper, get_0, nullsub/nopsub stubs, unload_resource, free_sdgame2, font_op2_alt, parse_shape2d_helper3.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Game C was compiled by Microsoft C 5.10, medium model, /O /Gs.
hypotheses.evidence: Every accepted C function is exact under this profile and independently re-verified under DOSBox-X; codegen families covered: long arithmetic helper calls, far/near pointers, register SI/DI locals, struct copies, boolean/char returns, nested guards, block-scoped slot reuse. Reinforced 2026-09-25 by profdisc: /O is the only tested MSC 5.10 optimization profile preserving all 31 frozen controls (alternatives 22-28/31). 2026-09-26: remains canonical default; per-object flag exceptions registered as TUFLAG-* (SUPPORTED, TU-specific).
hypotheses.explains: All accepted C.
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: Does not (yet) explain symptoms S1-S6; they are not attributed to the profile until an explanation is proven.
hypotheses.reopen_if: An alternative profile preserves (nearly) all accepted_c controls with explained exceptions AND fixes recurring residuals across unrelated functions with new strict matches.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Microsoft C 5.00 compiler with the same flags instead of 5.10.
hypotheses.evidence: Identical output to 5.10 for all accepted functions tested and for the pad_id, file_get_shape2d, parse_shape2d_helper, mmgr and RPM probes.
hypotheses.controls: accepted_c (full set per prior validation); probe sets above
hypotheses.explains: Same as 5.10.
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: Nothing observed; also fixes none of S1-S6.
hypotheses.reopen_if: A source/idiom is found where 5.00 and 5.10 codegen differ; then test it against the image.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Statically linked runtime is the MSC 5.10 medium-model library set (MLIBCR/LIBH).
hypotheses.evidence: 12 complete runtime members bind exactly to pinned 5.10 archives; abs.c, ldiv.asm, uldiv.asm exist only in the 5.10 form (5.00 LDIV/ULDIV are 165/103 bytes with an __aFulmul fixup vs 156/97 in the image). runtime2 (fixup-aware scan, 2026-09-25): 45 diagnostic member extents covering 6,851 image bytes; 38 have identical 5.00/5.10 payload+FIXUPP, 7 match ONLY 5.10 members. Scratch binder reproduced _itoa, _ultoa, alshr.asm exactly.
hypotheses.explains: The 725 pinned runtime bytes.
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: Fixup-bearing members not yet canonical owners (integration pending); DGROUP data for many members unresolved.
hypotheses.reopen_if: A runtime region is found that matches neither library version.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Runtime library is the MSC 5.00 set.
hypotheses.evidence: 5.00 abs, ldiv, uldiv differ from the image bytes (sizes/fixups above). Nine other members are byte-identical between versions and do not discriminate.
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: abs, ldiv, uldiv.
hypotheses.reopen_if: Evidence of a mixed library set (e.g. a patched 5.00 archive).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Medium memory model (far code, near data, DGROUP).
hypotheses.evidence: RETF epilogues, 9A far calls with segment relocations, DGROUP-relative data offsets in all accepted C; runtime from medium-model archives.
hypotheses.explains: All accepted code.
hypotheses.reopen_if: Never for game C absent a contradiction in accepted controls.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stack checking disabled (/Gs).
hypotheses.evidence: No __chkstk calls in accepted C; omitting /Gs on the pad_id probe adds a stack-check call (62 vs 58 bytes).
hypotheses.explains: Prologues without __chkstk.
hypotheses.reopen_if: A C-framed game function with a __chkstk call is found (would indicate a TU-specific flag).

hypotheses.hypothesis: A different optimization switch (/Ox, /Ol, /Oi, /Os, /Od, /Gs omitted) fixes pad_id when the loop counter is declared `register`.
hypotheses.evidence: pad_id register-int source emits the same 58-byte output (sub sp,2 + NOP) under /AM /O, /AM /Gs, /Ox, /Ol, /Oi, /Os; omitting /Gs adds __chkstk.
hypotheses.controls: pad_id probe only (not a control set)
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: pad_id stays 58 vs 54 bytes.
hypotheses.reopen_if: Does NOT cover plain (non-register) int counters; see FLAG-Ol-plain-counter.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Global profile includes loop optimization (/Ol, e.g. /Ox or /Olt) which enregisters plain int loop counters without a BP home (explains S1).
hypotheses.evidence: profdisc controlled matrix (486 runs, 31 frozen accepted controls with full extents, recipe fixups, bindings, ordered relocations): /Ol and /Olt emit the same objects as /O for plain-int counters in pad_id, audio_enable_flag6, audio_disable_flag6 (counter stays in memory); /Ox and /Oalt put the counter in SI but RETAIN the BP home (60/54, 58/52, 70/62 bytes). No alternative gives any exact match. tuflags: globally still FALSIFIED; TU-specific /Oa+/Ol (within /Ox) SUPPORTED for seg027 (TUFLAG-Ox-seg027).
hypotheses.controls: accepted_c frozen 31: /O 31/31; /Ol 28; /Olt 28; /Ot /Ol 28; /O /Ot /Ol 28; /Oa 25; /Oal 23; /Oalt 23; /Ox 22. /Ol family breaks init_carstate_from_simd (614/618), locate_many_resources (bytes 0x1a-0x22), parse_shape2d_helper3 (0x19: c4 vs 8b).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hand-written modules were assembled by a specific assembler/version.
hypotheses.evidence: Linked bytes (encodings, pads, jump sizes, frames) do not distinguish MASM 4.0/5.0/5.1, TASM or inline assembly; original OMF signatures are stripped by EXEPACK. MASM 5.x is the natural first hypothesis (MSC 5.10 era, supplied startup ASM sources); MASM 4.x and TASM remain live. No assembler pinned; the user must supply a specific legally held distribution with version/hash before any ASM contribution can be tested. Local pinned toolchain/msc510-msdos/MASM.EXE is Microsoft Macro Assembler 5.10 (1988), SHA-256 1c6286c69b616160b8475ad17453ee872702a2c98075c2159ec792a1c745275f, not yet in an active profile. Alternatives being provisioned under C:	ools. 2026-09-25: provisioned under C:	ools from pinned PCjs commit bd4cc85928f2291c8d08e610038a1dd70b94ac6c: MASM 4.00 (runner stack overflow under MS-DOS Player), 5.00, 5.10, 5.10A, 6.00 (DOS ML.EXE from disk 2). MASM 5.00/5.10/5.10A emit identical 78-byte smoke objects. TASM 1.0/2.0 not available on PCjs. Control experiment `asmdisc` (reassemble pinned library ASM sources vs Microsoft library objects) in progress. User supplied Borland TASM 1.0, 1.01, 2.0, 2.01 (winworldpc disk images) under C:	ools; being extracted/provenanced to C:	ools	asm-*. gather also collected MASM 2.04/3.00/3.01/6.11 and MSC 2.03/3.00/4.00/6.00AX/7.00 (local copies). asmdisc: readable MASM sources for game routines video_get_status, timer_get_counter, kb_checking reproduce their complete oracle extents under all six assemblers (MASM 4.00, 5.00, 5.10, 5.10A, pinned 5.10, ML 6.00) â€” the ASM contribution path is feasible but these probes do not discriminate. TASM not yet tested (asmdisc2). Discriminating constructs known from library controls: AND reg,imm sign-extended imm8 encoding (MASM 4.00 vs 5.x), EXTDEF ordering, COMENT checksum, IF1/IF2 support (ML 6.00). asmdisc2 (14 sampled game ASM extents + alignment control, 10 assemblers): MASM 5.00/5.10/5.10A/pinned 5.10 and TASM 1.00/1.01 match 14/14; MASM 4.00 13/14 (encodes AND BX,0Fh as 81 E3 0F 00 vs game 83 E3 0F -> FALSIFIED for game modules); ML 6.00 8/14 (DISFAVORED); TASM 2.00/2.01 default 7/14, 14/14 only with /jNOSMART plus local SMART regions (DISFAVORED: contortion). Library controls: TASM 0/14 and 0/12. Remaining NON_DISCRIMINATING set for game ASM: {MASM 5.00, 5.10, 5.10A, TASM 1.00, 1.01}. Next discriminator: FIXUPP record order vs oracle MZ relocation order (asmdisc3). SUPERVISOR RULING 2026-09-26: canonical ASM contribution profile = already-pinned toolchain/msc510-msdos/MASM.EXE (MASM 5.10) because every tested game ASM routine is byte-identical under MASM 5.00/5.10/5.10A and TASM 1.00/1.01; this is a reproduction profile, NOT a provenance claim; status stays NON_DISCRIMINATING and any routine/OMF evidence separating these candidates reopens it (and may switch the profile). 2026-09-26: ASM contribution path canonical (integ12); 14 game routines (685 B) accepted as matching ASM under the pinned MASM 5.10 reproduction profile, incl. symptom functions file_get_shape2d, file_get_res_shape_count, sprite copies, timer_compare_dx. 2026-09-27 integ25: pinned LINK 3.65/3.61 preserve each object's FIXUPP order; pinned MASM 5.10 emits ascending FIXUPPs, matching the seg012 ASM modules' ascending oracle runs; but the seg007 region, frame_callback_replay_group and seg037 have DESCENDING runs per record (MSC-like) -> their MASM 5.10 reproductions were demoted. REOPENED for these regions: experiment 'asmorder' tests other assemblers (TASM 1.0x, MASM 4/5.0/5.1A/6) and the C hypothesis. asmorder 2026-09-27: every available assembler (MASM 3.00/3.01/4.00/5.00/5.10/5.10A, ML 6.00, TASM 1.00/1.01/2.00/2.01) emits ASCENDING FIXUPPs -> the descending-run regions (seg007, frame_callback, seg037) are compiler output, not assembler output. Order discriminates: TASM 1.x puts forward-referenced loader fixups at record end and FAILS 3 accepted modules (graphics_resource_runtime/132056/137138) -> TASM 1.x FALSIFIED for game ASM; MASM 5.00/5.10/5.10A remain NON_DISCRIMINATING.
hypotheses.controls: Pinned runtime ASM members (known MASM-assembled library objects) serve as encoding controls.
hypotheses.reopen_if: FIXUPP/relocation-order test (asmdisc3) or another construct separates MASM 5.x from TASM 1.x.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The executable was produced by one normal run of pinned MSC 5.10 LINK (3.65) followed by pinned EXEPACK (4.06).
hypotheses.evidence: Diagnostic single-LINK fixture: two untouched accepted C objects (mat_mul_vector2, set_frame_callback) among synthetic raw OMF placeholders placed exactly; LINK load image equals the oracle prefix; EXEPACK output equals all 200,000 oracle bytes (oracle SHA) with the 3 live relocations in oracle order. LINK relocation order = input-object order, then FIXUPP subrecord order within an object (not address-sorted); EXEPACK regroups into 64 KiB banks (runs 1205/903/476/4). Zero-length early far-data segment declarations were needed in the synthetic fixture (not yet historically explained). relorder: EXEPACK 4.06 stably partitions LINK relocations by 64 KiB bank (crossed-bank control [140016,60003,140020,70009] -> [60003,70009,140016,140020]); within-bank order preserved, cross-bank interleaving lost, so object boundaries are only partially recoverable. MSC 5.10 FIXUPPs descend within each CODE LEDATA (across function boundaries) and LEDATAs advance in address. Grouped unload_resource/locate_shape_alt/locate_text_res probe reproduces oracle relocation indices 1759-1761 in exact order (TU-membership evidence for those three). objmap: /DOSSEG places 16 null bytes at _TEXT start [117842,117858) (entry IP 0x12); relocation order recovers link processing order (seg000..009, crt0..signal, seg011, seg012 modules interleaved with seg013..037).
hypotheses.controls: 2 accepted C objects; 3 of 2,588 relocations live.
hypotheses.explains: Image layout and relocation coordinate form (EXEPACK rewrites LINK pairs).
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: 2,585 relocations not yet produced from real fixups; entry CS:IP and stack not reproduced in the fixture.
hypotheses.reopen_if: A full fixture with real fixups produces an order LINK cannot generate from any object order.

hypotheses.hypothesis: MSC 5.10 /O word-aligns EVERY function in an object: an odd-length function is followed by one 90 NOP whether it is the last function or not.
hypotheses.evidence: relorder canonical-profile multi-function probes emit CB 90 CB 90 (second public at offset 2); isolated odd-length probes also end with 90.
hypotheses.explains: An odd-length TARGET with NO following 90 pad was not followed by MSC per-function alignment: its successor is not MSC C in the same object (ASM/data/other object with byte alignment) or the target itself is not MSC C. An intervening 90 alone is NOT a TU boundary.
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: Earlier claim (functions inside one object are not individually padded) is FALSIFIED; extra-NOP residuals (mmgr_alloc_a000, mmgr_get_chunk_size_bytes, polarRadius3D) therefore do not indicate same-TU successors. asmorder: holds for MSC 5.x /Ot-style padding only; MSC 6.00A /Os pads neither functions nor object tail (seg007).
hypotheses.reopen_if: An accepted multi-function MSC object shows unpadded odd-length interior functions.

hypotheses.hypothesis: An F3-prefixed string instruction (rep movs/stos, repe cmps) in game code is not output of the pinned C compilers; it marks hand-written (or library) assembly.
hypotheses.evidence: 20-run probe matrix (CL 5.00, CL 5.10, QCL 1.00, QCL 1.01 x /O,/Od,/Ox,/Oi,/O /Oi): every emitted REP string op uses F2, including 29-60 byte aggregate copies, near/far, far globals, /Ox loop-to-REP conversion and inlined memcpy; _fmemcpy/movedata stay external calls. Image: every game F3 A4/A5/AA/AB site lies in a procedure listed as an ASM proc in the reference seg012 listing; F3 also occurs in pinned MASM-built runtime members (_strcat, _strcpy F3 A4/A5; _strcmp F3 A6) and in start/__setargv. kbdoc 2026-09-26 (docs/msc510-codegen.md): PARTLY CONTRADICTED â€” MSC 5.10 intrinsic strcmp/memcmp emit F3 A6 (repe cmpsb), also under plain /Oi or #pragma intrinsic; F3 movs/stos (F3 A4/A5/AA/AB) never observed from MSC. Marker holds only for F3 A4/A5/AA/AB.
hypotheses.controls: mat_mul_vector2 (accepted C) uses F2 A5 for its struct copy; pinned runtime ASM members use F3.
hypotheses.explains: S3 and every F3 string-op site as class-7 positive evidence (with other markers), not a profile difference.
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: F3 A6 is NOT an ASM marker (MSC intrinsic strcmp/memcmp). AUDIT: any ASM acceptance whose positive evidence was only F3 A6 must be re-reviewed.
hypotheses.reopen_if: A pinned C compiler/profile is shown to emit F3 for some source form.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Startup is the pinned MSC 5.10 dos\crt0.asm member.
hypotheses.evidence: 197 startup code bytes match at load 0x1CC62 outside 24 fixup spans; its 11 relocation sites occupy consecutive oracle indices 2023-2033. runtime2: MZ entrypoint and both startup anchors identify 5.10 MLIBCR.LIB dos\crt0.asm at [117858,118055) with 24 fixups, followed by a 5,369-byte run of 22 complete library code segments [118056,123425).
hypotheses.explains: Startup code block.
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: Full 88-byte DATA, 2,048-byte STACK contribution, CS:IP, 8,000-byte final stack and an unusual COMENT checksum not yet proven.
hypotheses.reopen_if: Its DATA/STACK contribution cannot be reconciled with the image.

hypotheses.hypothesis: 80186/80286 code generation (/G1 or /G2) explains pad_id's smaller frame.
hypotheses.evidence: /G1 and /G2 make pad_id 54 bytes only by using ENTER/LEAVE; the target uses push bp/mov bp,sp and mov sp,bp. No ENTER/LEAVE observed in accepted controls.
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: Wrong instructions.
hypotheses.reopen_if: ENTER/LEAVE found in game code.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A single 00 byte between an odd-length procedure and the next even-aligned one is LINK segment-alignment fill between OBJECTS (MSC's own intra-object pad is 90), i.e. evidence of an object/module boundary after a non-MSC-padded (typically ASM or runtime) contribution.
hypotheses.evidence: extents audit: exact pinned member lengths/hashes place the trailing 00 after _strcat, _strcmp, _strlen, _strrchr, __aFlshr OUTSIDE their CODE members; asmmap: 4/11 adjacent pinned-module edges have a one-byte 00 pad; set_fontdefseg's reference listing has explicit `align 2; db 0`. MSC 5.10 /O pads odd-length functions with 90 inside the object (relorder). objmap: 00 fill after ret before even start consistent with all 9 resolved seg012/C interleave boundaries; none contradicted.
hypotheses.explains: Where object boundaries fall after odd-length non-C contributions; helps segment the image into modules for the TU/link plan.
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: An explicit ASM `db 0`/align directive inside a module can also produce 00; a 00 pad does not by itself identify the assembler.
hypotheses.reopen_if: A 00 pad is found inside a single proven object.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Canonical MSC 5.10 /O allocates automatic-local BP homes by walking a 16-bucket symbol hash table: bucket = (sum of the first 31 identifier bytes) & 15; buckets in ascending order; within a bucket newest declaration first; each local at its even-rounded size (char/int/near ptr one word, long two). Parameters keep ABI homes, statics take none, explicit register locals still get a home. Nested scopes allocate independently and reuse a freed home from a LIFO free pool only if large enough (no split/coalesce); a containing scope releases its direct homes then descendants in lexical preorder. Register assignment: explicit eligible `register` candidates receive SI then DI in DECLARATION order within active scopes (independent of the hash order used for BP homes); pushes follow the used registers.
hypotheses.evidence: hashrule: predictor build/workers/hashrule/slotorder.py matches 360/360 synthetic local-address mappings, 37/37 synthetic frame extents, and 19/19 addressable automatic-local homes across 14 accepted source files (frame size 13/14; init_carstate_from_simd has 4 bytes of compiler-generated index temporaries not modeled). Use/declaration-order and function-name changes do not move homes except within a bucket. regrule: 55/55 probe assignments, 58/58 probe push sequences, 20/20 accepted functions' save order (all 6 with explicit register declarations); 12 SI/DI accepted sources re-verified strictly. Extended predictor: build/workers/regrule/slotorder.py (diff slotorder-register.diff).
hypotheses.controls: pinned profile only; accepted rect_adjust_from_point (sibling-block sharing).
hypotheses.explains: Slot-order residuals are resolved by choosing readable names that hash to the needed buckets (suggest_names()), not by artificial structs.
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: Compiler-generated temporaries and spills are outside the model.
hypotheses.reopen_if: Two same-named-local sources with different slot orders under identical scope structure.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The restunts-numbered seg012 region (218 small procedures, 21.8 KB: file/sprite/font/shape/mmgr/kb/timer/video utility library) is predominantly hand-written assembly, with at most thin C-compatible wrappers.
hypotheses.evidence: Every game F3 string-op procedure (MARKER-F3-string-op) is in seg012; 11/12 unexplained S2/S5/S6 symptom functions are in seg012; S6 XOR zeroing is emitted by no pinned Microsoft compiler (MSC 5.00/5.10/6.00A, QuickC); shared-tail entries, CS-resident sprite data, cld;lodsb scans, direct I/O, EA thunks and 00 alignment pads cluster there; only 3/218 procedures are accepted C (thin wrappers whose bytes an assembler would also produce). Function-specific positive evidence (dlr-2): draw_line_related_alt writes the live [bp-4] byte of draw_line_related's frame and jumps into its shared body (not expressible in MSC C); in-code switch tables alone are NOT an ASM marker (MSC C switch emits jmp cs:[bx+table]).
hypotheses.controls: Accepted C elsewhere; pinned MASM-built runtime members share the markers.
hypotheses.explains: Why C search stalls across seg012; routes seg012 to the ASM contribution path (asmdisc/asmdisc2).
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: Some seg012 members may still be C (e.g. wrappers); the reference listing's ASM form is not proof.
hypotheses.reopen_if: Several non-trivial seg012 procedures match canonical C exactly.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Microsoft assembled the MSC 5.10 runtime/startup library objects with MASM 5.00.
hypotheses.evidence: asmdisc: reassembling 14 MSC 5.10 library ASM sources (STARTUP, STARTUP/DOS, SOURCE; /Dmem_m, /Mx) â€” MASM 5.00 core-OMF exact 14/14 (THEADR and LIB member A3 comment excluded); MASM 5.10, 5.10A and pinned 5.10 13/14, differing only in dos\crt0 COMENT A2 checksum (target and MASM 5.00 emit invalid D1, 5.10 emits valid D2). MASM 4.00: payload-exact on 12 assembled 5.10 controls but no core-OMF match; on MSC 5.00 controls it differs in AND SP,FFFEh encoding (81 E4 FE FF vs 5.x 83 E4 FE) and EXTDEF order. ML 6.00 rejects IF1/IF2 CMACROS.
hypotheses.explains: CRT0's unusual COMENT checksum (closure roadmap); runtime rebuild-from-source path.
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: Says nothing directly about the assembler used for the GAME's hand-written modules.
hypotheses.reopen_if: A 5.10 library member is found that only MASM 5.10 reproduces.

hypotheses.hypothesis: MSC 5.10 folds constant index offsets into the address displacement: arr[i-16] with 76-byte elements is emitted as [i*76 + (arr-1216)], so an instruction's DGROUP displacement can lie before the object it accesses.
hypotheses.evidence: dataext: sub_3771E-area code indexes base 0x81FC with stride 76 and an index bound 16..23, so all accesses fall exactly in [0x86BC,0x895C) starting at the reference label 0x86BC (8 x 76). Not yet confirmed by a compiled exact match. foldidx compiled probes (canonical profile): 76-byte arr[i-16] -> FIXUPP to _arr with encoded addend 40 FB (-1216); field +2 -> 42 FB (-1214); arr[i+3] -> E4 00 (+228); 2-D row indexing -1216; SoA word indexing -32; 608-byte outer row -9728. Image scan: 2 procedures use the folded 0x81FC displacement with guards 16..23 and stride 76 (sub_3771E, audio_init_chunk2).
hypotheses.explains: Displacements that appear to reach before/after an object; justifies a stride+bound-proven addend rule instead of coalescing labels.
hypotheses.reopen_if: The compiled natural form emits a different displacement/fixup.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Pinned MSC 5.10 supports source-scoped `#pragma intrinsic(inp, outp, inpw, outpw, _enable, _disable)`, emitting direct IN/OUT/CLI/STI instead of far calls.
hypotheses.evidence: intrin probes under canonical /AM /O /Gs.
hypotheses.controls: in-source pragma leaves accepted sources unaffected
hypotheses.explains: Direct port I/O and CLI/STI are NOT by themselves positive hand-ASM markers; they can come from C with this pragma.
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: Did not explain audio_add_driver_timer/audio_remove_driver_timer (their descending relocation order resets between functions; grouped C emits one descending LEDATA run).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Global /Oi (intrinsics for all TUs) is part of the game profile.
hypotheses.evidence: intrin: /Oi reproduces direct intrinsic expansion without pragmas but preserves only 30/31 frozen accepted contributions (is_facing_camera fails ordered FIXUPP validation). An in-source #pragma intrinsic explains the same codegen without breaking controls. tuflags: per-TU /Oi (via /Ox) supported for seg027 only. kbdoc: `#pragma intrinsic(memcpy|strlen|strcpy|strcat|strcmp|memset|abs)` placed AFTER the prototype inlines these under canonical /O (C2164 arises only when the pragma precedes the prototype). Intrinsic use can therefore come from source pragmas, not flags: TUFLAG-Ox-seg027/seg030 remain reproduction sets but /O+pragma is a NON_DISCRIMINATING alternative for the intrinsic part (tools/preprocessor.py currently blocks these names â€” tooling gap).
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: Breaks is_facing_camera.

hypotheses.hypothesis: MSC 5.10 CODE LEDATA record closes after the instruction/unit that brings it to >=944 bytes (hard cap 949 incl. 2-byte offset), or right after the unit carrying the 99th FIXUPP; a jcc+3 followed by a near jmp is one unit; each switch-table word is one unit.

hypotheses.hypothesis: MSC 5.10 /O keeps fewer common-subexpression temporaries in a function once the translation unit has referenced more distinct external symbols / static data / string literals before and inside that function; unreferenced declarations, labels, locals, name lengths and later functions have no effect.
hypotheses.evidence: s003c 2026-09-27: update_frame (seg003) exact only with fewer distinct referenced externs before/in it (sweep build/workers/s003c/mergesweep.py, ctx16-ctx33, pt_*.c); one extra referenced extern near the limit breaks exactness. s000c 2026-09-27: in seg000 the compiler leaves a dead `pop si` at the end of end_hiscore under internal-table pressure (label count, LENGTHS of referenced extern names); renaming externs to address-alias names removes it -> extern NAME LENGTHS are observable in codegen. Explains security_check's odd start 0x44CF (fallthrough byte, no pad; padding inside security_check shows the compiler saw the odd start) â€” not a post-link patch. s003d: cost model measured with full-TU compiles: each referenced file-scope extern ~24 B + name length (arrays/functions ~+4); the current function's local and parameter names count (2-byte resolution); NOT counted: unreferenced declarations, struct field names, prototype parameter lists, DOS environment size, earlier functions' locals/code, globals first used after the affected code; data externs declared inside an earlier function are freed at its end, called functions are not. Regime ladder in update_frame's three j2 loops (cached j2*2/j2*4 at [bp-154]/[bp-150]). Files: build/workers/s003d/knob.py, kinds.py, headroom.py, envtest.py, scan_*.txt. s005c: the budget is function-global (references added even at the function's tail remove earlier CSEs), includes labels and function definitions; the CSEs it removes go in a fixed order; the two seg005 residuals (setup_car_shapes y_pos CSE, loop_game temp slot) are NOT reachable by adjusting pressure (tests pressure.py, rename_probe.py). patterns 2026-09-27 (build/workers/patterns/REPORT.md, rules.json): codegen is a NON-MONOTONIC step function of the symbol-table budget (bands): seg000 exact for dP -14..+2 or >=+16 name chars, fails +4..+14 or <=-16; loop_game exact for relief >=588 (else temp slot [bp-44h] 0-252, no CSE 256-584); seg003 (semantic names) exact for relief 520-880; seg001 insensitive (-900..+400). Budgets add across names within ~20 chars; one pass-directory character ~= one name character. loop_game residual IS pressure: declaring setup_car_shapes' 20 private data externs inside it (K&R, freed at function end) makes loop_game exact. typenames: data DEFINED in the TU counts toward the budget like referenced externs (namefit model fix; prediction then matched seg000's window). MSC 5.10 pushes char arguments int-extended even with a char prototype, so call sites cannot reveal char prototypes. blocklift: near a pressure limit, brace/line LAYOUT inside a function changes codegen (moving `{` onto its own line at 20+ sites changed loop_game); blank lines do not. Source text must never be re-rendered/reformatted once exact.
hypotheses.explains: why whole-TU context (earlier members, merged declarations) changes a function's code; why stubbing other bodies (blockdiff --stub-others) can mislead near the limit
hypotheses.fails_or_breaks: makes declaration granularity AND extern name lengths observable; RULING: names must be natural semantic names (Restunts/semantic spellings), never lengths tuned by meaningless names.
